topics.title: 1.6. The Shape of Ethiopia and its Implication (የኢትዮጵያ ቅርፅ እና አንድምታው)
topics.topics:
Countries of the World have different kinds of shape that can be divided into five main categories. These shapes have implications on defense, administration and economic integration.

💡 ፈተና ላይ፡ የቅርፅ አይነቶችን ከነ ምሳሌያቸው (ለምሳሌ: South Africa = Perforated, Chile = Elongated) እንዲሁም የ Compactness መለኪያዎችን (ለምሳሌ፡ B/C Ratio ወደ 1 ሲጠጋ ምን ማለት እንደሆነ) በደንብ ይጠይቃሉ።
topics.content:
**Shape Categories (የቅርፅ አይነቶች):**
• Compact shape (የተሰበሰበ/ድቡልቡል ቅርፅ): The distance from the geographic centre to any of the borders does not vary greatly. It is easier for defence, socioeconomic and cultural integration.
• Fragmented shape (የተበታተነ ቅርፅ): Divided from their other parts by either water, land or other countries.
• Elongated shape (የተለጠጠ/ረጅም ቅርፅ): Geographically long and relatively narrow like Chile.
• Perforated shape (የተበሳሳ/በውስጡ ሌላ ሀገር የያዘ ቅርፅ): A country that completely surrounds another country like the Republic of South Africa.
• Protrude shape (ጉልህ/ወደ ውጭ የወጣ ቅርፅ): Countries that have one portion that is much more elongated than the rest of the country like Myanmar and Eritrea.

**Compactness Indices (የመጠቅለል መለኪያዎች):**
• Area-Boundary (A/B) ratio: The ratio of area of country to its boundary length. The higher the ratio, the greater the degree of compactness.
• Boundary-Circumference (B/C) ratio: The ratio of boundary length to the circumference of a circle having the same area. The nearer the ratio to 1, the more compact the country is.
• Area-Circumference (A/C) ratio: The ratio of the area to the circumference of the smallest inscribing circle. The higher the ratio, the greater the degree of compactness.
• Area-Area (A/A') ratio: The ratio of the actual area to the smallest possible inscribing circle. The nearer the ratio to 1, the more compact the country is.

**Table 1.3: Ethiopia's shape compared to its neighbors in the Horn**
- Ethiopia: Area=1,106,000 | Boundary=5,260 | A/B=210.27 | B/C=1.41 | A/C=296.61
- Djibouti: Area=22,000 | Boundary=820 | A/B=26.83 | B/C=1.56 | A/C=41.83
- Eritrea: Area=117,400 | Boundary=2,420 | A/B=48.51 | B/C=1.99 | A/C=96.83
- Kenya: Area=582,644 | Boundary=3,600 | A/B=161.85 | B/C=1.33 | A/C=215.28
- Somalia: Area=637,657 | Boundary=5,100 | A/B=125.03 | B/C=1.80 | A/C=225.22

topics.title: 1.7. Basic Skills of Map Reading (የካርታ ንባብ መሰረታዊ ክህሎቶች)
topics.topics:
A map is a two-dimensional scaled representation of part or whole of the Earth surface on a flat body. Map reading encompasses a systematic identification of natural and manmade features.

💡 ፈተና ላይ፡ Map Reading ምን ምን ነገሮችን (Natural vs Manmade features) መለየት እንደሆነ እና የካርታን አጠቃላይ ጠቀሜታዎች (Importance of map) በ True/False ወይም Multiple Choice ይጠይቃሉ።
topics.content:
**Importance of Maps (የካርታ ጠቀሜታዎች):**
• Provide the basis for making geographical details of regions represented (relief, drainage, settlement).
• Powerful tools for making spatial analysis of geographical facts.
• Useful for giving location of geographical features using grid reference and place naming.
• Used across various disciplines like land use planning, military science, aviation, tourism, epidemiology, etc.
• Makes storage of the geographical data of areas represented.
• Potentially used to assess reliable measurements of geographical features.

topics.title: 1.8. Types of Map and Marginal Information (የካርታ አይነቶች እና መግለጫ መረጃዎች)
topics.topics: 💡 ፈተና ላይ፡ Topographical እና Statistical map ልዩነታቸውን፤ እንዲሁም Marginal information (Scale, Key, North Arrow) ምንነትንና ጥቅምን በደንብ ያዙ።
topics.content:
**Types of Map (የካርታ አይነቶች):**
• Topographical maps (የገፅታ ካርታዎች): Depict one or more natural and cultural features. Can be small, medium or large scale. Contents depend on purpose, scale, date of compilation, and nature of the land.
• Special purpose/statistical maps (ልዩ/የስታቲስቲክስ ካርታዎች): Show distribution of different aspects such as temperature, rainfall, settlement, vegetation.

**Marginal Information (መግለጫ መረጃዎች):**
• Title (ርዕስ): Heading of the map which tells what the map is all about.
• Key/legend (መፍቻ): List of all conventional symbols and signs shown on the map with their interpretation.
• Scale (ስኬል/መጠን): Ratio between the map distance and actual ground distance (representative fraction, statement/verbal, linear/graphic).
• North arrow (የሰሜን አቅጣጫ ጠቋሚ): Indicated with the north direction; used to know other important directions (east, west, south).
• Margin (ማዕቀፍ): The frame of the map showing the end of the mapped area.
• Date of compilation (የታተመበት ቀን): Date of publication enabling users to realize whether the map is updated or outdated.

topics.title: 1.9. Basic Principles of Map Reading (የካርታ ንባብ መሰረታዊ መርሆዎች)
topics.topics: 💡 ፈተና ላይ፡ Grid Reference System እንዴት ቦታን በትክክል ለማግኘት (Pinpoint location) እንደሚረዳ መገንዘብ ወሳኝ ነው።
topics.content:
**Principles (መርሆዎች):**
• Visualizing Symbols: Readers must translate map symbols into landscape images. The first symbols introduced should refer to familiar landscape features.
• Knowledge of Directions: Essential to orient and locate places. The north arrow should be determined first before locating features in relation to one another.
• Grid Reference Systems: Maps are covered in a series of lines that make up a grid with numbers. These numbers provide a grid reference to accurately pinpoint a location.
